newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ICB Shipping H1 pre-tax profit down 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: ICB Shipping H1 pre-tax profit down 10 pct.

text.p: Sweden's ICB Shipping AB said on Monday pre-tax profit in the first half of 1997 fell 10 percent and said it expected the tank market to improve over the next few years.
The company said pre-tax profit fell to 151 million crowns in the first half of the year from 168 million in the same 1996 period.
The higher figure for the first six months of 1996 reflects a 168 million crown gain from ship sales compared to zero in the first half of 1997.
Turnover rose to 469 million crowns from 421 million.
"Rates for ICB's ships in the first half of the year were better than in the same period one year ago," ICB said in its results statement.
It said rates for VLCC rose 16 percent to around $30,000 per day and for Suezmax ships 24 percent to $27,000 per day.
"ICB forecasts that the tank market will improve more in the coming few years," it said.
Currency effects and a 23 million crown one-off gain from Knightsbridge Tankers Ltd lifted the result.
A credit of of 69 million crowns due to currency effects compared to a charge of two million crowns in the same period a year earlier boosted the result, it said.
ICB said rising demand for cargo capacity would probably boost rates in the next few years.
"Demand for tonnage is rising gradually while deliveries of new ships will be limited in the next few years, which should give scope for continued rates rises," ICB said.
Net worth rose to 99 crowns per share at mid-year from 83 crowns on December 31 and 76 crowns on June 30, 1996.
ICB Shipping acquired six percent of the shares in Knightsbridge Tankers Ltd during the period. ICB Shipping will administer Knightsbridge Tankers for an annual fee of $750,000, ICB Shipping said.
ICB Shipping's share was changing hands at 91.5 crowns at 1130 GMT, down 0.50 crowns, while the Stockholm Stock Exchange's general index was down 0.21 percent at 3,172.71
